# The planning board

The board is the source of objectives and tasks. Everything the web page does goes through
its JSON API. The service is private to the LAN. No authentication. Reference: `GET /api/docs`
(HTML) or `GET /openapi.json`. Ids are plain numbers in the API (task 43), written `T43` for
tasks and `O12` for objectives in pages and briefings only.

## Rules

- Send `X-Actor: <your team>` on every write; it is recorded in the history. The names are one
  list, used for who owns a task, who wrote an item or a note, and who made a change: `John`,
  `platform`, `plc`, `memory`, `simulator`, `infra`, `cyberplanetary`, `sonalon`, `brand`,
  `cosmogenitor`, `concepts`, `business`, `devops`, `planner`. Use the team whose folder you work in
  (`devops` works in `/cosmoshot/tools`).
  Without the header the actor is `John`. Use the same name as `author` on notes.
- Read before you act: `GET /api/state` (the whole board) or one briefing, see below.
- Work is recorded as notes on its task. Set the task `in progress` when you start. Set `done`
  only when the task says you close it; otherwise leave it for whoever assigned it.
- Do not move objectives between lanes, delete anything, or change other tasks' dependencies
  unless asked. If a task is wrong, say so in a note.
- Task status is one of `not started`, `in progress`, `done`, `dropped` (anything else: HTTP 400).
- Note text starts with the time: `[2026-11-15 12:03 EST] ...` from `date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M %Z'`.

## Calls

    B=https://cosmoshot.benac.dev
    curl -s $B/api/context/task/43.md                      # briefing: task, notes, what it depends on
    curl -s "$B/api/context?tasks=43,44&mode=brief"        # several items, mode full|brief|item
    curl -s $B/api/state                                   # everything, JSON
    curl -s -X PATCH $B/api/tasks/43 -H 'X-Actor: <your team>' \
      -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"status":"in progress"}'
    curl -s -X POST $B/api/tasks/43/notes -H 'X-Actor: <your team>' \
      -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"author":"<your team>","text":"[TIME] what I did"}'

Task fields you may PATCH: `title`, `detail`, `who` (the owner: `John` or a team from the list above), `kind`, `status`, `size`, `high_priority`.
When you create a task (POST /api/tasks) you must send `high_priority`: `true` if the task must be
finished before its objective counts as met, `false` if it is optional (the objective can be met
and move to Done while it is unfinished). The call is refused without it. A write that is
accepted answers 200 with the whole board plus `change` (the history entry that undoes it).
Errors are HTTP 400 or 404 with `{"error": "..."}`.

## Dry run and undo

- Add `?dry_run=1` to any write: the server runs it in a transaction, describes the effect
  (`title`, `lines`, `destructive`) and rolls back. Use it before anything that deletes or merges.
- `GET /api/history?limit=20` lists changes (`id`, `actor`, `summary`, `can_reverse`).
- `POST /api/history/<id>/reverse` puts one change back exactly (refuses if the touched rows
  changed since). It also takes `?dry_run=1`.

## Notes for tools

- Pass `--cacert /etc/ssl/centroid-ca/certs/ca-root.crt` to curl on a machine that does not
  already trust the Centroid Root CA (this host does).
- Use `/usr/bin/python3` for any script; the `python3` on PATH sometimes hangs.
